title: BlueSprig Logistics - Ops Onboarding Orientation
summary: Kickoff orientation for BlueSprig Logistics onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covered deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial pilot scope, security/compliance questions (SOC2, KMS, SAML), acceptance criteria for pilot (latency, cost), and next steps for SOW, bench tests, and data access. Action items assigned for SOW, security pack, pilot schedule, and initial benchmark tokens set.
next_steps: Maya to send draft SOW and pricing matrix by 2027-02-14
Diego to provision test model runbook and bench script by 2027-02-16
Customer to share sample traffic profile and dataset links by 2027-02-12
Schedule 2-hour hands-on benchmark with SREs on 2027-02-18
action_items: Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Send draft SOW & pricing sheet - due 2027-02-14
Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE): Create bench script and initial KV cache config - due 2027-02-16
Ravi Patel (CSM): Upload onboarding runbook template and schedule weekly check-ins - due 2027-02-11
Tom Benson (BlueSprig): Share egress/ingress network diagrams and service account details - due 2027-02-12
Sara Liu (BlueSprig): Confirm required retention window and encryption policy (KMS) - due 2027-02-13
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, I run customer success for this region, um, and with me are Ravi our CSM and Diego our solutions engineer. Good morning, Asha, Tom, Sara, Ken. Can you hear us okay?
[00:10] Asha (BlueSprig): Yeah, hi Maya, thanks. We're excited to get started. Morning team.
[00:15] Tom (BlueSprig): Morning. Quick note, we have folks on PST and CET so we're juggling calendars.
[00:20] Maya: Totally, we'll keep the agenda tight. Quick run-through: goals for today — alignment on pilot scope, security controls, what success looks like, and immediate next steps. Ravi, want to add?
[00:31] Ravi (CSM): Just to emphasize handoffs — we'll run weekly 30-min syncs and a technical bench with Diego. Also uploads for runbooks, ops playbooks.
[00:39] Diego (SE): Hi all, real quick on my side: I'll dig into the traffic profile you shared in the intake form, and prepare a bench harness. I may ask for smaller sample traces if possible.
[00:48] Priya (BlueSprig): Thanks. For context, BlueSprig runs real-time routing decisions for last-mile deliveries; we care about p95 latency under load, and cost per million tokens is a factor, obviously.
[00:59] Maya: Great. Can you confirm stakeholders and SLOs? Asha?
[01:05] Asha: Sure. Stakeholders: Product (Priya), Platform (Tom), SRE (Ken), Legal/Privacy (Sara). SLOs — p95 end-to-end inference < 300ms for 512-token requests, and target inference spend so that q1 pilot cost < $15k. Also need PII controls and audit trails.
[01:23] Maya: Noted. We should discuss deployment preferences — hosted API to move fast vs Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private for tighter network control. Tom, what's your leaning?
[01:33] Tom: Initially we prefer Hosted to iterate, but for production we may need VPC/private because of residency and egress policy. We also have compliance constraints — SOC2 and an internal encryption policy that requires customer KMS.
[01:44] Diego: We can support that path: start hosted, then Dedicated or Private with VPC peering. Note though the ded- — sorry, Redwood Dedicate — the Dedicated pools give you isolated GPU capacity and predictable latency, and for Private we can do a private control plane.
[01:59] Ken: One of the key things for us is key management. Does Redwood integrate with KMS/HSM and can we bring our own keys?
[02:07] Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; we'll share the security pack. Sara, any particular compliance checklist items?
[02:14] Sara (BlueSprig): We need audit logs retention 1 year, SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC for token access, and proof of SOC2 compliance. Also need to understand data-at-rest and in-transit encryption and logs visibility.
[02:26] Ravi: We'll attach our SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc. For logs, Redwood Console exposes per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns — Diego will demo in the bench.
[02:38] Diego: On observability, we can push traces to your tracing backend; we also export latency histograms and token counts. There's an agent or webhook you can plug in.
[02:47] Priya: How much data do you retain by default for prompts/outputs? We have to make sure we don't keep customer PII longer than necessary.
[02:55] Maya: Default retention is 30 days but can be configured; for Private deployments you can choose zero retention. We'll confirm in the security pack.
[03:05] Asha: Pilot scope — what do we need to prove in next 4 weeks?
[03:10] Maya: Good question. Suggested pilot milestones: 1) Integration + connectivity ok (week 1), 2) Bench results for throughput and latency (week 2), 3) Cost modeling and optimization recommendations (week 3), 4) Final evaluation against SLOs and go/no-go (week 4). Thoughts?
[03:27] Tom: That timeline is tight but doable if we collaborate. We'll need Diego to run bench with our SREs and maybe a synthetic trace to simulate traffic.
[03:35] Diego: I'll prepare bench harness that simulates bursty, tail-heavy traffic and includes KV cache patterns. We should test with both 256 and 512 token contexts, and a small quantized model for cost sim.
[03:47] Ken: We need to understand autoscaling config — how long to spin up extra pods and the cost hit for sudden spikes.
[03:54] Diego: Autoscaling behavior depends on Dedicated pool settings; default cooldowns are 60s but we can tune. For Hosted we have cold-start smoothing and warm pools.
[04:02] Priya: Any known gotchas with tokenization differences or model variants that could affect output quality?
[04:08] Diego: Yes, model variants and quantization can change perplexity and sometimes response phrasing; Redwood Optimize will flag regressions based on prompt evals we run. We'll include model/repro steps in the runbook.
[04:19] Asha: On legal, procurement might ask for a data processing addendum and terms for liability. Whom should we loop in?
[04:26] Maya: Our legal contact is Elise Morales — I'll introduce her once the SOW is shared. We'll also provide a standard DPA and SOC2 pack.
[04:34] Sara: Also want to confirm network setup — we prefer VPC peering for Dedicated; do you support private endpoints?
[04:41] Diego: Yes, we support VPC peering and PrivateLink-like endpoints on major cloud providers. For on-prem, we have a packaged deployment but that will need more lead time.
[04:50] Tom: About metrics, is there a way to get token-level cost per route and break down by model version? We want to attribute cost to product lines.
[04:59] Ravi: Yes, Redwood Console can break down by route and model. We can also export CSVs for finance.
[05:06] Priya: For the bench, what model should we start with? We currently use a small Llama-based model internally for prototypes.
[05:12] Diego: We recommend starting with a mid-tier quantized open model that matches your latency needs; I'll propose three model variants in the bench plan: a low-latency small model, a mid model tuned for quality, and a fallback cheaper variant.
[05:25] Asha: What's the average p95 we should expect on Hosted for 512 tokens on comparable hardware?
[05:30] Diego: On our hosted profiles, p95 for 512 tokens on an A100-class shard is typically 180-300ms depending on batch size and batching window. But with aggressive batching for cost we sometimes see higher latency; we'll tune batching versus immediate latency.
[05:47] Tom: Can Redwood do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes?
[05:53] Maya: Yes, rollouts and fallbacks are supported. You can set A/B traffic splits, canaries, and automatic fallback policies in the console.
[06:01] Ken: We also want to keep a replay log for failed responses for debugging — retention for that?
[06:06] Ravi: Replay logs are configurable; we'll default to 7 days but can extend. We'll document best practices.
[06:12] Priya: Ok, can we talk about authentication — API keys vs mTLS? We might want mTLS for Private.
[06:19] Diego: We support API keys, OAuth, and mutual TLS for private endpoints. For SSO we use SAML + SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:27] Maya: Quick checkpoint — seems like everyone is aligned on starting hosted pilot then evaluating Dedicated/Private for prod. Agree?
[06:33] Asha: Yes, agreed.
[06:35] Tom: Agreed, hosted to start.
[06:37] Maya: Great. Let's put some specific acceptance criteria on the board now — Asha?
[06:43] Asha: Pilot success means: p95 < 300ms for 512 tok at target 200 RPS synthetic load, quality pass rate > 90% on our prompt set, and estimated monthly cost projection within 15% of our target. Also security checklist items must be documented and KMS confirmed.
[07:00] Diego: We'll run bench with those exact parameters and provide a report with histograms, percentiles, and cost per million tokens.
[07:09] Priya: What about throttling behavior when traffic exceeds Dedicated capacity?
[07:13] Diego: You can set burst capacity and fallbacks; when capacity is exhausted the system can route to a cheaper variant or return rate-limit responses. We'll document fallback policy options.
[07:24] Sara: On data residency, we need EU-region support for a subset of traffic. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
[07:30] Maya: Yes, you can route requests by region; we also support regional model variants where needed. We'll include region routing options in the runbook.
[07:38] Tom: Any caveats about KV cache behavior across nodes and warm starts? We rely on small prefixes for repeated queries.
[07:45] Diego: KV cache is node-local unless you use shared cache settings; cold starts will miss cache. We'll test prefix hit rates in the bench and provide guidance on warm pooling and cache sizing.
[07:56] Asha: Time for logistics — what do you need from us this week to kick the pilot?
[08:01] Maya: Top items: sample prompt set (10–20 representative prompts), traffic profile (RPS distribution), network diagrams, and contact for SREs. If you can share by Friday 2027-02-12 we'll hit week-1 integration.
[08:13] Tom: We'll share those. I'll send network diagrams and a service account for testing.
[08:18] Sara: I'll confirm retention and encryption policy by Monday.
[08:22] Maya: Awesome. Any other questions?
[08:25] Priya: Slight question on cost modeling: do you charge for KV cache storage separately?
[08:30] Ravi: Cache is part of the serving cost but there are specific price deltas for large persistent caches in Dedicated; we'll include in pricing matrix.
[08:39] Diego: Also, for quantized models there may be a small accuracy delta. Optimize will give recommendations when regression thresholds hit.
[08:46] Asha: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[08:49] Maya: Recap: Maya sends SOW & pricing by 2/14; Diego bench script by 2/16; BlueSprig shares prompts, traffic, network by 2/12; schedule hands-on benchmark on 2/18. Ravi to schedule weekly check-ins starting 2/11.
[09:05] Ken: One last ask — can we get a sample of your runbook and incident escalation path?
[09:10] Ravi: Yes, I'll upload the onboarding runbook and an oncall escalation doc to the shared drive after this call.
[09:16] Maya: Perfect. Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the security pack.
[09:22] Tom: Thanks. Bye.
[09:25] Maya: Bye everyone.
